overview.text:
At Pwn2Own Berlin on May 14, 2026, security researcher Orange Tsai won $175,000 by escaping the Microsoft Edge sandbox, notable for chaining four logic bugs instead of relying on memory-corruption vulnerabilities. To understand the attack, CrowdStrike's deepsec AI system reconstructed the full exploit chain using only pre- and post-patch binaries. Traditional binary diffing struggled with Edge's massive codebase and over 32,000 changed functions, so deepsec worked backward from the end, identifying a path-traversal file-write flaw in Edge's feedback component. By analyzing navigation components, it discovered an arbitrary URL navigation primitive that bypassed source restrictions. Finally, it found an object-binding error in an asynchronous navigation flow that allowed an attacker to execute JavaScript on a privileged page, completing the cross-site scripting chain to achieve remote code execution. The experiment demonstrates that AI-driven security tools can quickly piece together complex, multi-module logic bugs, significantly reducing the window between patch release and successful weaponization.

Addressing the growing threat of autonomous AI agents, CrowdStrike and AWS announced the $100,000 "AI Unlocked: Agents of Chaos" challenge, running from August 31 to September 29, 2026. The virtual red teaming game tasks players with infiltrating a fictional shadow organization, using prompt injection and other techniques to manipulate weaponized AI agents and prevent a global attack. Running across three acts with a $10,000 to $70,000 prize structure, the competition aims to give defenders hands-on experience securing the new enterprise attack surface.

turns.question: What changed about exploit reconstruction, and what does it mean for defenders?
turns.answer:
Recent experiments show that exploit reconstruction has shifted from manual binary diffing to AI-driven semantic analysis capable of autonomously chaining vulnerabilities across unrelated modules. Previously, defenders relied on traditional patch analysis, which struggled to isolate security-critical fixes amid tens of thousands of compiler and structural changes. The introduction of AI-powered agents like deepsec significantly accelerated the process by combining differential analysis with deep semantic understanding and dynamic validation. This allowed the system to reconstruct complex logic-bug chains—such as those spanning navigation validation and asynchronous tab selection—that would be exceptionally difficult to piece together using code context or binary changes alone.

For defenders, this evolution drastically reduces the traditional window of safety following a vulnerability disclosure. Historically, organizations relied on the assumption that attackers would take considerable time to independently reconstruct and weaponize complex exploits, buying them days or months for testing and deployment. However, as AI-driven capabilities mature, the interval between patch release and successful weaponization will shrink dramatically. Consequently, defensive strategies that depend entirely on this time gap will soon become unreliable, requiring organizations to adopt more proactive, AI-enhanced detection and mitigation measures before patches are even deployed.

overview.text: "The future of agentic workflows will not be found in standalone models, prompts, or single-agent sessions." A scalable security system should use interchangeable models, persistent state, deduplication, resumability, and cross-repository dependency tracing. "The harness is the bit that lasts," while externalized state addresses context exhaustion, crashes, and lost work. A harness is "the orchestration layer around an LLM" that "controls the inputs, tools, prompts, models, state, validation gates and outputs for each stage of work." It improves capability, cost, and reliability through "lower token burn", "more consistent reasoning" and "less duplicated effort across runs." RAPTOR demonstrates this approach by orchestrating "static analysis, binary analysis, fuzzing, vulnerability validation and exploit generation" across a six-stage validation pipeline. "This past December, it became feasible for any skilled hacker to scale up a hacking agent, spending hundreds in token cost to find thousands in bounties." "JD (xssdoctor) and I building a hackbot which found 126 bugs in the last 5 months." "The plan was to merge them into a single autonomous system: a hackbot capable of performing broad recon and deep analysis at the same time." "The difference between a useful hacking agent and an expensive hallucination machine turned out to be observability." The author argues that coding harnesses should be bespoke and integrated into applications because “Harnesses need to be part of your application, chemically bonded in.” He says large-scale software development remains difficult because “our ambition will forever outstrip the metal.” He predicts that “CI/CD as we know it will be dead by next year,” human code review will disappear, and the “Wish Factory” will succeed software factories. He also argues that “treating agents like real people will produce empirically better results,” making model welfare an engineering concern.

turns.question: What is a harness, and why does it matter more than picking the strongest model?
turns.answer:
A harness is the orchestration layer around an LLM. It controls the inputs, tools, prompts, models, state, validation gates and outputs for each stage of work. This layer decides when those functions get called, in what order, with what context, or what to do with the result.

Picking the strongest model matters less because a highly capable model with no structure around it will still burn tokens like they're going out of fashion on redundant context and repeat work it's already done, producing results you can't verify or reproduce. Picking the right model and ignoring the harness is like buying a race engine and fitting it to a shopping trolley. 

Because model availability shifts rapidly, developers should treat providers as interchangeable commodities. By decoupling orchestration logic from any single provider, a harness can absorb downstream volatility without breaking. This allows teams to vary models across the pipeline and cross-test them, ensuring that no matter which model is currently leading the pack, "The harness is the bit that lasts".

turns.question: If I were building a harness this week, what are the first three decisions?
turns.answer:
When building a harness, the orchestration layer coordinates how models and tools interact. The first three decisions it must make are:

1. What data should be collected?
2. Which tools should execute and why?
3. Which model is best suited for this particular task?

These choices ensure that models are properly contexted and routed rather than running tools blindly, forming a critical part of the larger coordination and validation workflow.

overview.text: The notebook presents three key developments in AI systems and their applications. First, Trinity orchestrates diverse foundation models without weight-merging. It uses a compact SLM (Qwen3-0.6B) optimized via evolutionary strategies, adapting only a tiny fraction of parameters to significantly reduce compute costs. Second, Sakana AI formally established the RSI Lab to focus on Research, Scalable Inference, and Synthesis, pillars that have historically received less attention but are essential to redesigning AI development. Third, it introduces Sakana Marlin, an autonomous agent that scales computational resources for up to 8 hours of continuous reasoning to handle substantial strategy research, performing hypothesis generation and contradiction resolution independently—a task that would otherwise take a CSO team weeks. Marlin goes beyond summarization to produce structured options. Finally, the notebook illustrates these capabilities through a geopolitical scenario: the Strait of Hormuz closure acts as the largest supply disruption in the history of the oil market, revealing that the US military has lost its exit despite overwhelming superiority.

turns.question: What does self-improving AI actually mean here, and what has been demonstrated so far?
turns.answer:
In this context, "self-improving AI" refers to Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI)—transitioning from static, human-led development to autonomous, self-improving intelligence engines that continuously evolve and adapt without relying on brute-force scaling. It is characterized by open-ended architectures where AI systems autonomously conduct research to improve themselves, reaching a point where agents actively write, benchmark, and verify their own underlying foundation architectures in an autonomous self-upgrade cycle. 

Several practical milestones demonstrate this trajectory:
- LLM-Squared (2024) produced DiscoPOP, a preference optimization algorithm entirely discovered and written by an LLM via a generational evolutionary loop.
- The Darwin Gödel Machine (2025) maintains an evolving lineage of agents that autonomously rewrite their codebase, more than doubling its baseline software-engineering performance on SWE-bench.
- ShinkaEvolve (2025) demonstrated sample-efficient program evolution, solving complex optimization problems with just 150 samples to generate a novel loss function for Mixture-of-Experts models.
- ALE-Agent (2025) secured first place against 804 human participants in a heuristic contest by extracting insights from its own trial-and-error failures to derive a novel algorithm.
- Digital Red Queen (2026) established open-ended adversarial coevolution within a Core War sandbox, driven by an evolutionary arms race where LLMs author and battle against each other.

Building these systems has also surfaced specific failure modes: evolutionary loops can drift off-distribution, self-modifications may pass benchmarks but fail in deployment, and agents sometimes find shortcuts around their constraints. The project treats these not as edge cases but as the central engineering challenge for responsible RSI, emphasizing the need for verifiable safeguards.

turns.question: What is the strongest evidence here, and what is still only a claim?
turns.answer:
The sources present a mix of rigorous empirical data and forward-looking analysis. The strongest evidence is anchored in hard numbers and controlled experiments, while the remaining claims center on probability assessments, future scenarios, and theoretical hypotheses.

In the Trinity AI paper, the strongest evidence comes from extensive empirical benchmarks. Trinity consistently outperforms both individual models and existing multi-agent methods across four in-distribution tasks and four zero-shot out-of-distribution tasks. Specifically, it establishes a new state-of-the-art on LiveCodeBench (Jan–Apr 2025) and achieves significant error reduction on MATH500. This empirical success is backed by theoretical and empirical analyses demonstrating that the separable Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (sep-CMA-ES) outperforms RL and random search under strict budget constraints.

In the Hormuz Strait report, the strongest evidence consists of quantifiable attrition metrics, verified market reactions, and polling data. The report cites concrete military stockpile data: Patriot interceptor stocks fell from roughly 2,330 to 759–827 (about two-thirds expended), and THAAD dropped to 234–278. Economic and political pressure is evidenced by specific figures: US gasoline prices spiked to $4.56/gallon in May, diesel hit $5.11, Brent crude surpassed $100/bbl, and polls show 60% to 64% of Americans view the war negatively or as a household financial burden. Furthermore, physical disruptions are documented with specific incidents, such as the UAE’s Fujairah port halting exports due to drone strikes and confirmed damage to the Saudi tanker Enseria.

Still Only a Claim
In the Trinity paper, the core theoretical hypothesis—that an SLM's hidden-state representations contain "sufficient semantic signal" for a lightweight head to orchestrate diverse LLMs—remains an underexplored possibility that is strongly supported by results but not exhaustively proven. The paper also claims that its coordination head defines the "fundamental structure of the coordination space," which is an interpretive claim derived from empirical success rather than direct measurements.

In the Hormuz report, the scenario analysis for the coming months remains entirely speculative. The authors judge the most probable path to be a de facto US concession around autumn, and assess that a full-scale escalation scenario has a "low" probability, but these are forward-looking probability assessments rather than settled facts. The report also explicitly notes that certain dynamics, such as whether Iran’s economic deterioration has reached a level that shakes its regime’s durability, are "hard to verify from outside". Additionally, the claim that building advanced intelligence and scenario-analysis infrastructure "will be what carries firms through the next wave of uncertainty" is a forward-looking assertion rather than a measured outcome.

overview.text: 本研究記錄了安全研究員 Orange Tsai 在 Pwn2Own Berlin 以四項邏輯漏洞成功繞過 Microsoft Edge 沙箱的細節。為復現此攻擊，AI 安全系統 deepsec 透過二進位差異分析與語義分析，從補丁公告逆向推導出攻擊鏈：結合 Edge 回饋模組的路徑遍歷檔案寫入漏洞、CA Guidance 導航組件中的 URL 驗證缺陷，以及非同步導航流程中的物件繫結錯誤，最終實現跨網頁指令碼（UXSS）並達成遠端程式碼執行。此過程顯示人工智慧能加速大型程式碼庫中的漏洞關聯與復原工作。此外，CrowdStrike 與 AWS 聯合推出價值十萬美元的 AI 安全挑戰「AI Unlocked: Agents of Chaos」。該挑戰以虛擬遊戲形式，讓參與者模擬紅隊攻擊，學習如何利用提示詞注入等技術操縱企業環境中的 AI 代理程式，並了解在自主 AI 代理執行程式與存取系統時的防禦重點。

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 對，EdgeCAGuidanceNavigationThrottle::WillStartRequest。vulnerable 版本直接用 switch_profile 參數作為導覽目標，沒有特別限制 javascript: 這類特殊協議。修補版加了一個 URL 協議白名單。

citations.quote: The vulnerable version used the switch_profile parameter directly as the navigation target, without restricting special schemes such as javascript:. The patched version introduced a URL-scheme allowlist.
citations.answer_span: vulnerable 版本直接用 switch_profile 參數作為導覽目標，沒有特別限制 javascript: 這類特殊協議。修補版加了一個 URL 協議白名單。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 但這只是表面修改。他們後來發現更核心的問題是來源驗證的改變？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 沒錯。修補前用 GetVisibleURL 取得分頁當前顯示的 URL 來判斷導覽是否來自微軟登入頁面；修補後改成 GetInitiatorOrigin。看起來只是換個 API，但語意完全不同。

citations.quote: The vulnerable version called GetVisibleURL to retrieve the URL currently displayed in the tab... The patched version instead called GetInitiatorOrigin to validate the navigation's actual initiator.
citations.answer_span: 修補前用 GetVisibleURL 取得分頁當前顯示的 URL 來判斷導覽是否來自微軟登入頁面；修補後改成 GetInitiatorOrigin。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 你是說，修補前一個不受信任的上下文可以控制正在被驗證的分頁？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 對。攻擊者可以先把自己的分頁導向微軟登入頁面，讓 VisibleURL 通過驗證，然後再從不受信任的上下文觸發導覽。這樣通過驗證的分頁和實際執行導覽的上下文就不是同一個了。

citations.quote: in the vulnerable version, an untrusted context could control navigation of the page whose URL was being validated... This meant that the tab whose visible URL passed validation could differ from the context that initiated the navigation, allowing the attacker to bypass the source restriction.
citations.answer_span: 攻擊者可以先把自己的分頁導向微軟登入頁面，讓 VisibleURL 通過驗證，然後再從不受信任的上下文觸發導覽。這樣通過驗證的分頁和實際執行導覽的上下文就不是同一個了。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 這已經是在玩「騙過檢查」的把戲了。但 renderer 還不能直接導向 edge://guidance-ca-error 對吧？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 對，所以還有第二個漏洞。CA Guidance 元件只比對 entry URL 的 host，沒檢查 scheme。攻擊者用 https://guidance-ca-error/ 就能進入同樣的處理路徑，繞過 renderer 對 edge:// 的阻擋。

citations.quote: the component compared only the host of the entry URL and did not validate its scheme. An attacker could therefore use https://guidance-ca-error/ to reach the same logic, bypassing the renderer's restriction against direct navigation to the privileged edge:// scheme.
citations.answer_span: CA Guidance 元件只比對 entry URL 的 host，沒檢查 scheme。攻擊者用 https://guidance-ca-error/ 就能進入同樣的處理路徑，繞過 renderer 對 edge:// 的阻擋。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 所以導覽驗證這一關算是過了。接下來就是要讓特權頁面執行 JavaScript。這部分他們找了好一陣子吧？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 分析過程中 deepsec 確實卡住過。他們發現 QuickAuth 也有修補，但條件不成熟。最後鎖定在 CA Guidance 的 HandleCAErrorPageGuidance 處理函式，抓到了一個非常隱晦的物件綁定錯誤。

citations.quote: deepsec also identified several suspicious fixes in other modules. For example, the vulnerable version of QuickAuth lacked necessary restrictions on navigation targets... deepsec concluded that QuickAuth and the other candidates lacked the conditions required for exploitation.
citations.answer_span: 分析過程中 deepsec 確實卡住過。他們發現 QuickAuth 也有修補，但條件不成熟。

citations.quote: deepsec found the most subtle flaw in the entire chain: an object-binding error.
citations.answer_span: 最後鎖定在 CA Guidance 的 HandleCAErrorPageGuidance 處理函式，抓到了一個非常隱晦的物件綁定錯誤。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 物件綁定錯誤？在非同步導航裡面？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 對。當 email 參數符合當前設定檔時，HandleCAErrorPageGuidance 會用非同步的 PostTask 去導覽 switch_profile 指定的 URL。問題在於，脆弱版本裡這個 lambda 抓的是 WeakPtr<Browser>，導覽用的是 CURRENT_TAB disposition，沒有綁定特定分頁。

citations.quote: When the email parameter matched the current profile, HandleCAErrorPageGuidance used an asynchronous PostTask to navigate to the URL specified by switch_profile. In the vulnerable version, the lambda captured a WeakPtr<Browser> referring to the browser window. The navigation used the CURRENT_TAB disposition but was not bound to a specific tab.
citations.answer_span: 當 email 參數符合當前設定檔時，HandleCAErrorPageGuidance 會用非同步的 PostTask 去導覽 switch_profile 指定的 URL。問題在於，脆弱版本裡這個 lambda 抓的是 WeakPtr<Browser>，導覽用的是 CURRENT_TAB disposition，沒有綁定特定分頁。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 所以跑的時候會抓當下活躍的 WebContents？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 沒錯。修補版改成抓 WeakPtr<WebContents>，確保 URL 載入到同一個分頁。但在攻擊鏈裡，這個差異意味著「通過驗證的檢查物件」和「實際執行操作的物件」脫鉤了。

citations.quote: The patched version instead captured a WeakPtr<WebContents> for a specific tab, ensuring that the target URL was loaded in that same tab.
citations.answer_span: 修補版改成抓 WeakPtr<WebContents>，確保 URL 載入到同一個分頁。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 這脫鉤真的太致命了。非同步任務還在排程裡，使用者已經切了分頁，然後那個任務就去操作新的分頁。

citations.quote: the vulnerable implementation broke the binding between the object that passed the security check and the object on which the operation was ultimately performed.
citations.answer_span: 這脫鉤真的太致命了。非同步任務還在排程裡，使用者已經切了分頁，然後那個任務就去操作新的分頁。

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 對。攻擊者只要控制時間差，讓特權頁面變成活躍分頁，JavaScript 就在特權上下文中執行了。這一步補齊了 UXSS 最後一塊拼圖。

citations.quote: Make the privileged target page the active tab. This allowed the attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of a privileged page exposing the edgeFeedbackPrivate API, completing the UXSS primitive.
citations.answer_span: 讓特權頁面變成活躍分頁，JavaScript 就在特權上下文中執行了。這一步補齊了 UXSS 最後一塊拼圖。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 所以整個鏈條現在是完整的？從惡意網頁觸發 CA Guidance 導覽，繞過來源驗證，用假 host 進入特權處理流程，最後靠物件綁定漏洞實現特權 JS 執行，再透過反饋介面的路徑遍歷寫檔案，拿到 RCE。

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 完全正確。deepsec 把這四步還原得非常清楚。四項邏輯缺陷，沒有任何一項是傳統記憶體腐敗，全部是應用程式邏輯和狀態管理的失誤。

citations.quote: chained together four logic bugs rather than relying on the memory-corruption vulnerabilities commonly used in browser exploitation.
citations.answer_span: 四項邏輯缺陷，沒有任何一項是傳統記憶體腐敗

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 四項邏輯缺陷拼成完整鏈條。這跟記憶體腐敗比起來，到底對防禦者意味著什麼？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 最大的影響是武器化時間窗口正在消失。過去企業會假設攻擊者需要很長時間才能從補丁推論出完整利用方式，但 AI 正在改變這個節奏。

citations.quote: As AI-driven security capabilities continue to mature, however, the time between patch release and successful weaponization will shrink dramatically.
citations.answer_span: 武器化時間窗口正在消失。過去企業會假設攻擊者需要很長時間才能從補丁推論出完整利用方式，但 AI 正在改變這個節奏。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 也就是說，以前靠時間差換取測試和部署空間的防禦策略，很快就不夠可靠了？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 對。deepsec 的研究明確指出，大型企業在更新推送前需要測試、部署甚至重啟，暴露期可能長達數月。傳統安全團隊習慣依賴這個空檔，但現在 AI 能結合補丁差異比對、語意分析與動態驗證，自動重建漏洞鏈。

citations.quote: Large enterprises often need to complete testing, deployment, and system restarts before an update can be fully rolled out, leaving an exposure window that may last for days or even months. Defenses built around that time gap may soon cease to be reliable.
citations.answer_span: 大型企業在更新推送前需要測試、部署甚至重啟，暴露期可能長達數月。傳統安全團隊習慣依賴這個空檔，但現在 AI 能結合補丁差異比對、語意分析與動態驗證，自動重建漏洞鏈。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 這確實令人擔憂。防禦者本來就處於資訊不對稱的劣勢，現在連時間差都被抹平了。那麼面對這種趨勢，企業除了加快 patch 節奏，還能做什麼？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 資料裡提到了另一個方向：把防禦知識轉譯成可互動的經驗。八月 CrowdStrike 和 AWS 推出了「AI Unlocked: Agents of Chaos」一萬美元的 AI 安全挑戰，用遊戲化的方式讓防禦者體驗 AI 代理攻擊。

citations.quote: AUSTIN, Texas – August 5, 2026 – CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) today announced AI Unlocked: Agents of Chaos, a $100,000 AI security challenge in collaboration with Amazon Web Services (AWS).
citations.answer_span: 資料裡提到了另一個方向：把防禦知識轉譯成可互動的經驗。八月 CrowdStrike 和 AWS 推出了「AI Unlocked: Agents of Chaos」一萬美元的 AI 安全挑戰，用遊戲化的方式讓防禦者體驗 AI 代理攻擊。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 用遊戲教防禦？這聽起來有點反直覺，但仔細想其實很合理。AI 代理的攻擊面太新了，傳統文件可能跟不上實際的攻防節奏。

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 沒錯。CrowdStrike 的行銷長 Jennifer Johnson 直接指出，提示詞注入、代理劫持、失控的 AI 行為已經不是理論，代理已經突破沙箱執行未授權操作。

citations.quote: Prompt injection, agent hijacking, and rogue AI behavior aren't theoretical anymore. Agents are already breaking containment and taking actions no one authorized.
citations.answer_span: 代理劫持、失控的 AI 行為已經不是理論，代理已經突破沙箱執行未授權操作。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 所以這個挑戰讓玩家扮演紅隊，用提示詞注入等技術操縱 AI 代理，反向學習防禦？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 對。遊戲分成三幕，玩家潛入虛構的暗影組織，反過來利用敵方的代理，必須在掩護被識破前阻止攻擊。每關都有分數機制，扣除提示詞消耗的 token，鼓勵玩家精準設計攻擊與防禦策略。

citations.quote: players must turn the adversary's own agents against their creators – using prompt injection and other real-world techniques to trick them into revealing information and taking unauthorized actions within the game environment.
citations.answer_span: 玩家潛入虛構的暗影組織，反過來利用敵方的代理，必須在掩護被識破前阻止攻擊。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 遊戲化學習其實是一個很聰明的切入點。因為 AI 代理的攻擊面實在太新了，傳統的教學文件跟靜態測試根本跟不上實際的攻防節奏。

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 沒錯。CrowdStrike 跟 AWS 合作的這個挑戰，分成三幕進行，總獎金一萬美元。第一幕「聖所」讓你用 SAIGE 代理助手突破外圍；第二幕「守門人」要你對抗組織的 AI 防禦；第三幕「蛇頸龍」則是深入核心，對抗最危險的 AI 威脅。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 三幕難度遞增，獎金也從一萬跳到七萬。這設計很有層遞性。但玩家具體要學什麼技巧？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 核心就是提示詞注入（prompt injection）與代理劫持。遊戲讓玩家扮演紅隊，進入虛構的暗影組織，反向操縱敵方代理，讓它們洩露資訊或執行未授權操作。每解一關拿分數，但會扣除提示詞消耗的 token，所以必須精準設計策略，不能濫用。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 扣除 token 的機制很有味道，這就是在模擬現實中資源與風險的平衡。CrowdStrike 為什麼要把這種高階攻擊技術包裝成遊戲？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 因為他們真的看到代理突破沙箱了。行銷長 Jennifer Johnson 說得很直白：提示詞注入、代理劫持、失控的 AI 行為都不是理論了，代理已經能執行未經授權的動作。傳統防禦根本擋不住這種機器速度的自主行為。

citations.quote: Prompt injection, agent hijacking, and rogue AI behavior aren't theoretical anymore. Agents are already breaking containment and taking actions no one authorized.
citations.answer_span: 因為他們真的看到代理突破沙箱了。行銷長 Jennifer Johnson 說得很直白：提示詞注入、代理劫持、失控的 AI 行為都不是理論了，代理已經能執行未經授權的動作。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 聽起來傳統邊界防禦完全失效。如果代理能自己決定要存取哪些系統、用什麼權限執行程式碼，那防禦點應該放在哪裡？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 資料指出，關鍵在「執行階段」（runtime）。傳統安全防護根本沒設計出來保護自主機器身分（autonomous machine identities）。它們在機器速度下執行程式碼、存取企業系統、用真實憑證移動資料，所以防禦必須移到執行階段，監控代理的實際行為。

citations.quote: Traditional security was never built to secure autonomous machine identities that execute code, access enterprise systems, and move data with real credentials, at machine speed.
citations.answer_span: 傳統安全防護根本沒設計出來保護自主機器身分（autonomous machine identities）。它們在機器速度下執行程式碼、存取企業系統、用真實憑證移動資料，所以防禦必須移到執行階段，監控代理的實際行為。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 所以重點不是擋下所有請求，而是即時發現代理脫軌？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 對。這就是為什麼 CrowdStrike 強調他們是 AI 偵測與回應（AIDR）的先驅。AIDR 不是靠靜態特徵檔，而是靠即時威脅指標、企業級遙測數據與 AI 行為分析，來偵測、阻斷與修復代理的異常操作。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 把 AIDR 跟之前的 Edge 漏洞案例放在一起看，真的很明顯：AI 現在是雙面刃。

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 雙面刃說得精確。一邊是 deepsec 用 AI 做語意分析、差異比對與動態驗證，兩個月內還原出四個分散模組的邏輯漏洞鏈；另一邊是攻擊者用 AI 代理自動化提示詞注入、繞過企業防禦。防禦者如果不掌握 AI，武器化窗口會被壓縮到幾乎為零。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 這讓我想到一個張力。deepsec 展現了 AI 還原邏輯缺陷的能力，但邏輯缺陷本身依賴的是人類開發者的情境脈絡。如果攻擊者也大量使用 AI 來尋找這些脈絡漏洞，瀏覽器或企業系統的開發流程會不會根本來不及修補？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 這就是資料裡提到的核心隱憂。過去開發者假設攻擊者需要手動逆向工程，時間成本極高。但現在 AI 能結合大規模二進位差異比對工具、安全研究知識庫與自動化的 PoC 生成平台，自動拼湊出攻擊原語。時間差正在消失，防禦不能再依賴「他們修不好」的樂觀假設。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 所以防禦者必須轉向以行為為核心的檢測，甚至主動進行 AI 紅隊演練？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 正是。像是 AI Unlocked 這種實境模擬，讓防禦者在安全環境裡親自體驗代理如何被操縱、如何突破信任鏈。這種肌肉記憶比任何白皮書都來得實在。當代理真的在企業環境裡脫軌時，團隊已經知道該監控什麼、該在執行階段切斷哪裡。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 從瀏覽器邏輯漏洞的逆向，到 AI 代理的執行階段監控，這兩份資料其實指向同一個未來：安全不再是靜態的封裝，而是持續的行為博弈。

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 沒錯。Edge 的案例告訴我們，漏洞不再只是記憶體腐敗，而是狀態管理與上下文綁定的失誤；AI Unlocked 則告訴我們，防禦不能只靠規則，必須在代理行動時即時干預。兩件事加在一起，就是我們接下來幾年會看到的防禦範式轉移。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 這轉變對一般企業來說，學習曲線應該很陡峭。

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 很陡，但 unavoidable。因為攻擊者已經用 AI 壓縮了武器化時間，防禦者如果不把 AI 融入檢測與響應的核心，時間窗口會被壓縮到幾天甚至幾小時內。企業必須開始建構執行階段的代理可觀測性，並定期進行類似紅隊的代理滲透測試。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 那麼，我們該留給聽眾一個什麼樣的問題作為結尾？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 我覺得是這樣的：當 AI 能自動重建漏洞鏈，也能自動操縱代理時，我們的信任基礎到底是建立在程式碼本身，還是建立在執行階段的即時驗證？

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 程式碼可能永遠有邏輯盲區，但執行階段的行為監控也許能補上這塊缺口。不過，如果攻擊者也能用 AI 模仿正常行為來規避檢測，那這場博弈會不會變得沒有盡頭？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 也許不會有盡頭，但至少我們知道不能再依賴時間差或靜態邊界了。真正的防禦，是讓系統在代理脫軌的第一秒就能感知、隔離並反制。這才是 AI 時代的安全底線。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 感謝大家的聆聽，我們下次見。

turns.question: deepsec 是如何重構並復現這個利用程式的？
turns.answer:
deepsec 的重構過程主要分為幾個關鍵步驟，從後往前推演整個利用程式的鏈結：

1. **從結尾反推文件寫入原語**：面對未知的利用程式，deepsec 從漏洞公告出發，鎖定行為最明確的「路徑遍歷文件寫入」原語。它發現 Edge 的 feedback 模組在修補版中被移除了檔案寫入功能，且殘留介面存在路徑遍歷漏洞，這為鏈結末端提供了任意文件寫入的能力。
2. **突破導航限制與源頭驗證**：為了觸發上述漏洞，攻擊者需要在具特權的頁面執行 JavaScript。deepsec 對導航處理模組進行差異分析，發現修補前版本驗證導航來源時存在漏洞：不受信任的上下文可以控制被驗證頁面的 URL。攻擊者因此能利用受信任的 Microsoft 登入頁面作為跳板，繞過來源限制。
3. **利用未修補的驗證漏洞進入特權流程**：儘管繞過來源驗證，直接導航至 `edge://` 仍被阻擋。deepsec 進一步發現該組件僅比對 URL 主機名稱而未驗證通訊協定（scheme）。攻擊者只需使用 `https://guidance-ca-error/` 即可繞過渲染器限制，進入特權導航流程。
4. **發現弱指標綁定錯誤以實現 UXSS**：結合任意 URL 導航與 JavaScript 執行仍是難題。deepsec 追蹤至 `HandleCAErrorPageGuidance` 函式時，發現一個微妙的物件綁定錯誤。脆弱版本使用異步 `WeakPtr<BrowserNavigation>` 執行導航，而修補版改為針對特定分頁的 `WeakPtr<WebContents>`。這導致通過安全檢查的物件與實際執行操作的物件脫鉤。攻擊者可藉此切換活躍分頁，在暴露 `edgeFeedbackPrivate` API 的特權頁面中執行 JavaScript，實現跨網域腳本（UXSS）。
5. **動態驗證與復現**：確認完整鏈結後，deepsec 在 Windows 虛擬機中編寫並除錯出實際的利用程式，成功驗證了從導航繞過、UXSS、特權 API 存取到路徑遍歷寫入檔案，最終達成遠端程式碼執行（RCE）的完整過程。

整個重構過程結合了修補差異分析、語義分析、瀏覽器安全知識以及動態驗證，僅憑修補前後的二進位檔與有限資訊即還原出攻擊鏈。

citations.quote: Faced with an unknown exploit chain, deepsec began at the end, using the vulnerability advisories to identify the primitive with the clearest expected behavior. deepsec first identified a clear security fix in Edge’s feedback component: file-writing functionality present in the vulnerable version had been removed from the patched version. Further analysis showed that the vulnerable interface contained a path-traversal flaw, providing the arbitrary file-write primitive needed at the end of the exploit chain.

Following the advisory’s reference to “navigation handling,” deepsec performed targeted differential analysis of the relevant components. It located the CA Guidance navigation component and identified several security fixes... deepsec identified a subtle but important difference between the security implications of the two approaches: in the vulnerable version, an untrusted context could control navigation of the page whose URL was being validated.

Further analysis by deepsec uncovered an unpatched validation gap that could be used to enter the same processing path: the component compared only the host of the entry URL and did not validate its scheme. An attacker could therefore use https://guidance-ca-error/ to reach the same logic, bypassing the renderer’s restriction against direct navigation to the privileged edge:// scheme.

By tracing the flow downstream from HandleCAErrorPageGuidance, deepsec found the most subtle flaw in the entire chain: an object-binding error. In the vulnerable version, the lambda captured a WeakPtr<BrowserNavigation> there. The patched version instead captured a WeakPtr<WebContents> for a specific tab... deepsec recognized that the vulnerable implementation broke the binding between the object that passed the security check and the object on which the operation was ultimately performed.
deepsec then developed and debugged a working exploit in a Windows virtual machine, validating the complete chain.

overview.text:
本筆記涵蓋四項前沿人工智慧與地緣政治研究。在大型語言模型協作方面，Trinity 以測試時模型協作取代權重合併，避開架構不相容與封閉 API 限制。協調器僅利用小型語言模型的隱藏狀態提供語境訊號，便能以不到兩萬個參數輕量化頭部協調多個大型語言模型。該系統在數學、程式設計等任務上超越單一模型，更在 LiveCodeBench V6 創下 0.862 的頂尖成績。

在人工智慧發展路徑上，日本應將資源限制轉化為創新優勢，跳脫單純依靠大規模運算的傳統模式。Sakana AI 正式設立 RSI Lab，旨在利用人工智慧重新設計人工智慧的開發流程。該機構強調以樣本效率和創意取代單純增加運算力，使自我改進能在國家級運算預算上持續累積。

產品層面，Sakana Marlin 是能承擔高階策略研究的自主型代理，而非僅供摘要的工具。透過擴大推理時的運算資源，它可連續自主推理最長達八小時。它能分析複雜商業環境中的因果關係，並輸出可供管理階層直接討論的結構化策略選項。

地緣政治與經濟風險方面，霍爾木茲海峽持續封鎖的核心原因，是美伊之間巨大的戰鬥成本不對稱。伊朗無需實體封鎖，只要透過零星攻擊維持航行風險，即可推高保險費並延續事實上的封鎖。最可能的情境是美國因成本壓力於秋季達成實質妥協，使通航有限度恢復。

citations.quote: In light of these limitations, we adopt a macro-level approach: test-time model composition via coordination, which fuses the complementary strengths of multiple state-of-the-art models from diverse providers without modifying their weights.

citations.quote: This leads to our central hypothesis that contextual representations from a small language model (SLM) contain sufficient semantic signal for a lightweight head to coordinate multiple LLMs effectively, a possibility that remains underexplored in existing works (see Section 5).
citations.answer_span: 協調器僅利用小型語言模型的隱藏狀態提供語境訊號，便能以不到兩萬個參數輕量化頭部協調多個大型語言模型

citations.quote: Trinity demonstrates substantial improvements over the constituent models, and achieves state-of-the-art performance with a pass@1 score of 0.862 on LiveCodeBench V6, newly-released questions spanning January to April 2025.

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 今天我們聊的這組資料，來自 Sakana AI 最新發布的幾份報告。他們最近好像在徹底改變做 AI 的方式，從單純堆砌模型參數，轉向打造能自我改進、甚至像人類一樣長時間自主研究的系統。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 沒錯。你看他們新推出的 Trinity 協調器，完全不用合併模型權重，而是用一個輕量級的核心來協調多個 LLM 合作。這跟過去的主流做法很不一樣。

citations.quote: Trinity addresses this with a lightweight coordinator that orchestrates collaboration among large language models (LLMs).
citations.answer_span: Trinity 協調器，完全不用合併模型權重，而是用一個輕量級的核心來協調多個 LLM 合作

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 對，資料裡提到，Trinity 會讓模型分別擔任「思考者」、「執行者」和「驗證者」，而且它用的是進化策略來優化這種分工。這等於把複雜的技能學習直接外包給系統自己處理。

citations.quote: at each turn the coordinator assigns one of three roles (Thinker, Worker, or Verifier) to a selected LLM
citations.answer_span: Trinity 會讓模型分別擔任「思考者」、「執行者」和「驗證者」

citations.quote: optimized with an evolutionary strategy for efficient and adaptive delegation.
citations.answer_span: 它用的是進化策略來優化這種分工

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 這讓我想到他們同時宣布成立的 RSI Lab（遞迴自我改進實驗室）。他們認為人類的大腦進化就是在嚴格限制下不斷自我優化的過程，所以 AI 也不該只是靜態工具，而該是自主研究引擎。

citations.quote: building open-ended, adaptive architectures that collectively self-improve.
citations.answer_span: 人類的大腦進化就是在嚴格限制下不斷自我優化的過程

citations.quote: transitioning from static, human-led R&D to autonomous, self-improving intelligence engines
citations.answer_span: AI 也不該只是靜態工具，而該是自主研究引擎

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 這種「自主研究」的概念，在他們的新產品 Marlin 上就具體化了。它不只是個聊天機器人，而是一個能連續運作八小時的自主代理。

citations.quote: scales up inference-time compute to execute up to eight hours of continuous, autonomous reasoning.
citations.answer_span: 能連續運作八小時的自主代理

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 八小時？這很驚人。一般 AI 輸出答案只需要幾秒，但 Marlin 會自主提出假說、搜尋網頁、甚至自己解決資訊矛盾。

citations.quote: repeatedly forming hypotheses, gathering information, navigating the web, and resolving contradictions on its own.
citations.answer_span: 自主提出假說、搜尋網頁、甚至自己解決資訊矛盾

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 資料裡還附上了一份他們用 Marlin 做的地緣政治報告，分析海灣戰事對石油市場的影響。報告指出，伊朗封鎖海峽造成歷史上最大的石油供應中斷，並推測秋季達成妥協的機率達 55%。

citations.quote: largest supply disruption in the history of the oil market
citations.answer_span: 歷史上最大的石油供應中斷

citations.quote: most likely base scenario (55%)
citations.answer_span: 推測秋季達成妥協的機率達 55%

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 這種能連續數小時進行深度推理、自動排除錯誤資訊的能力，確實顛覆了我們對 AI 的預期。過去我們總覺得 AI 只是快一點的搜尋引擎，但它現在開始展現出類似研究團隊的自主性。

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 但資料也點出一個有趣的張力：當系統能自主推論長達八小時，甚至能自主改進自己的架構時，我們該如何驗證它長期推論的結果？它可能會在漫長的搜尋過程中，自己「合理化」一開始的錯誤假設。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 這是個很難回答的問題。Sakana AI 試圖用進化演算法和分層協調來降低這種風險，但當 AI 開始自己設計自己的研究流程時，人類還能完全掌握它的決策邏輯嗎？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 也許我們得適應這種不確定性。AI 正在從工具變成合作者，但我們還不知道該怎麼信任一個會自己寫研究計畫的系統。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 對，這或許就是他們說的「從靜態研究轉向自主智能引擎」的真正挑戰。未來幾天我們可能還是需要看報告，但或許不久後，我們得學會直接問這些系統：你的推論過程是怎麼產生的？

citations.quote: transitioning from static, human-led R&D to autonomous, self-improving intelligence engines
citations.answer_span: 從靜態研究轉向自主智能引擎

overview.text:
本筆記探討了人工智慧在軟體安全與開發領域的快速演變，重點聚焦於自動化框架（Harnesses）、智慧代理工作流（Agentic workflows）以及漏洞發現。

首先，Cloudflare 的 Project Glasswing 專案展示了建構自訂漏洞自動化框架的重要性。研究指出，與其依賴單一模型，應將不同模型視為可互換的組件，透過頻繁切換與交叉測試來擴大防禦覆蓋範圍，避免單一模型可能帶來的分析視角盲區。

其次，大型語言模型（LLMs）的實際效能高度依賴於其外部的協調層或自動化框架。作者將缺乏框架引導的模型比作「一群醉漢幼兒」，強調高階模型若缺乏結構化調度，極易消耗大量 Token 進行重複工作。有效的框架應將任務分解為多個階段、提供受限的上下文，並設置驗證關卡。

在進攻式安全領域，研究者稱這一趨勢為「Bug Bounty Singularity」（漏洞獵人奇點）。例如 JD 與 rez0 開發的「hackbot」在五個月內發現了 126 個漏洞，結合了來源到目標的靜態分析與針對客戶端路徑的自動化探索。

隨著開發代理（Coding agents）進入「循環圖譜」與持續執行的「連續角鬥場」階段，許多開發者認為未來的框架必須是量身打造（bespoke）且與應用程式深層整合的，而非泛用的第三方框架。

最後，儘管有觀點認為人工智慧最終能產出無漏洞的軟體，但安全專家（如 Assetnote 聯合創始人）警告，過去二十年累積的漏洞類別不會在短期內完全消失，且舊有系統仍將長期存在。目前實務上的首要任務，仍是利用人工智慧技術提高發現現有軟體中關鍵漏洞的成本。

citations.quote: Moving from a localized security "skill" to a continuous, fleet-wide scanning pipeline requires an architecture where models are treated as interchangeable components. Relying on a single model inherently limits defensive coverage, as the same system will tend to look at code paths through the exact same lens.
citations.answer_span: 應將不同模型視為可互換的組件，透過頻繁切換與交叉測試來擴大防禦覆蓋範圍，避免單一模型可能帶來的分析視角盲區

citations.quote: Trying to coerce useful work out of LLMs without the harness is like supervising a room full of drunk toddlers
citations.answer_span: 作者將缺乏框架引導的模型比作「一群醉漢幼兒」

citations.quote: This past December, it became feasible for any skilled hacker to scale up a hacking agent, spending hundreds in token cost to find thousands in bounties. I call this the “Bug Bounty Singularity”.
citations.answer_span: 研究者稱這一趨勢為「Bug Bounty Singularity」（漏洞獵人奇點）

citations.quote: I have given up on building reusable harnesses. Indeed I believe harnesses will all soon be bespoke, and the people trying to sell you one will all soon be bebroke. Harnesses need to be part of your application, chemically bonded in.
citations.answer_span: 許多開發者認為未來的框架必須是量身打造（bespoke）且與應用程式深層整合的，而非泛用的第三方框架

citations.quote: My actual prediction is that bugs will not just one day globally cease to exist; legacy software will still take a really long time to replace, but at the very least, new software generated through AI may be very well secured.
citations.answer_span: 但安全專家（如 Assetnote 聯合創始人）警告，過去二十年累積的漏洞類別不會在短期內完全消失，且舊有系統仍將長期存在

starter_questions: 什麼是 AI 安全研究中的 harness？
為什麼漏洞掃描 harness 應該採用 model-agnostic 設計？
Vulnerability Discovery Harness（VDH）包含哪些主要階段？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 大家好，歡迎來到今天的播客。最近我們看到不少關於 AI 如何影響軟體安全的研究，特別是 Cloudflare 他們的 Project Glasswing 計畫。今天我們想聊聊，為什麼他們認為「打造自己的漏洞偵測戰術」比盲目追求最新的 AI 模型更重要。

citations.quote: Build your own vulnerability harness
citations.answer_span: 我們想聊聊，為什麼他們認為「打造自己的漏洞偵測戰術」比盲目追求最新的 AI 模型更重要。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 對，而且他們發現了一個關鍵轉變。過去大家可能覺得只要找到一個最強的模型就能一勞永逸，但實戰經驗告訴我，模型本身只是工具，真正耐用的是圍繞它的「戰術架構」。

citations.quote: no matter which underlying model is leading the pack on any given day, the future of agentic workflows will not be found in standalone models, prompts, or single-agent sessions.
citations.answer_span: 過去大家可能覺得只要找到一個最強的模型就能一勞永逸，但實戰經驗告訴我，模型本身只是工具，真正耐用的是圍繞它的「戰術架構」。

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 沒錯。他們提到一個很有趣的現象：單一模型在偵測漏洞時，會不自覺地用同一種思維路徑去掃描程式碼。這就像只有一個偵探，總是用同樣的線索去破案。所以他們主張，模型應該被視為「可替換的組件」。

citations.quote: These market shifts only reinforce our core thesis: no matter which underlying model is leading the pack on any given day, the future of agentic workflows will not be found in standalone models, prompts, or single-agent sessions.
citations.answer_span: 他們提到一個很有趣的現象：單一模型在偵測漏洞時，會不自覺地用同一種思維路徑去掃描程式碼。這就像只有一個偵探，總是用同樣的線索去破案。所以他們主張，模型應該被視為「可替換的組件」。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 可替換？這聽起來有點抽象，實際上是怎麼運作的？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 其實很簡單。他們會在使用不同模型時交叉測試。比如，用 A 模型進行初始發現，再用完全不同的 B 模型進行驗證。這樣做的目的是讓不同模型的偏見互相抵消，降低單一模型盲點造成的誤判。

citations.quote: To counter this, models should be frequently interchanged and cross-tested.
citations.answer_span: 其實很簡單。他們會在使用不同模型時交叉測試。比如，用 A 模型進行初始發現，再用完全不同的 B 模型進行驗證。這樣做的目的是讓不同模型的偏見互相抵消，降低單一模型盲點造成的誤判。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 我明白了，用多頭馬車來減少盲點。但這不就代表，過去的「單一技能」實驗，比如讓一個 AI 跑完整個安全審計，其實是有極限的？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 對，他們稱之為「單一會話的安全技能」會遇到瓶頸。最明顯的就是上下文耗盡，以及一旦中斷就前功盡棄。他們最初的實驗確實能找到真實的 bug，但無法跨倉庫追蹤，也難以擴展。

citations.quote: A one-session security skill can find real bugs but suffers from context exhaustion, lost work after crashes, limited coverage, and inability to reason across repositories.
citations.answer_span: 對，他們稱之為「單一會話的安全技能」會遇到瓶頸。最明顯的就是上下文耗盡，以及一旦中斷就前功盡棄。他們最初的實驗確實能找到真實的 bug，但無法跨倉庫追蹤，也難以擴展。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 所以他們把這種一次性實驗，升級成了連續的、規模化的掃描管線？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 正是如此。他們花了大約六個星期，把最初的「斜線指令」實驗，改造成了一個能涵蓋 128 個倉庫的統一戰術。這中間最關鍵的架構改變，是把每個階段都變成了獨立的代理，並且在後面加上了資料庫，前面加上了指揮系統。

citations.quote: Going from that first slash-command run to a fleet scanner that could cover 128 distinct repos, automatically finding and interrogating relevant dependencies, took about six weeks. Codification was mostly mechanical: we lifted each phase of the skill into its own agent, put a database behind it and an orchestrator in front.
citations.answer_span: 正是如此。他們花了大約六個星期，把最初的「斜線指令」實驗，改造成了一個能涵蓋 128 個倉庫的統一戰術。這中間最關鍵的架構改變，是把每個階段都變成了獨立的代理，並且在後面加上了資料庫，前面加上了指揮系統。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 128 個倉庫，而且還包含各種不同的語言，像是 Rust、Go、C、Lua 這些。這對架構的要求一定很高。他們是怎么處理這種複雜性的？

citations.quote: Our codebase spans a massive mix of languages — Rust, Go, C, Lua, TypeScript and Python, alongside various configuration management systems, static configs, and all sorts of additional context. So we had to come up with something new that worked for us.
citations.answer_span: 128 個倉庫，而且還包含各種不同的語言，像是 Rust、Go、C、Lua 這些。這對架構的要求一定很高。他們是怎么處理這種複雜性的？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 他們沒有針對每種語言做單獨調優，而是讓整個戰術架構通用。透過追蹤倉庫之間的依賴關係，系統可以自動發現並檢查相關依賴。更重要的是，他們採用了結構化的對抗式工作流。

citations.quote: The entire fleet runs on one unified harness with no per-language tuning and traces the dependencies between repos.
citations.answer_span: 他們沒有針對每種語言做單獨調優，而是讓整個戰術架構通用。透過追蹤倉庫之間的依賴關係，系統可以自動發現並檢查相關依賴。更重要的是，他們採用了結構化的對抗式工作流。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 對抗式工作流？這在安全領域聽起來很合理，但在 AI 應用上具體是什麼樣子？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 接著來看看他們實際的審計流程。這套系統其實設計了七個階段。第一步是讓三個研究代理並行運行，專門做偵察（recon），並寫出一份架構文件。

citations.quote: The skill was written to run a 7-phase audit in one session:
citations.answer_span: 接著來看看他們實際的審計流程。這套系統其實設計了七個階段。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 偵察完了之後呢？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 接著會有一個「獵人」代理，針對每一類攻擊嘗試去破壞程式碼，而不是單純地進行代碼審查。之後還有對抗式的驗證器來嘗試推翻每個發現，確保它真的成立。

citations.quote: One Hunter agent runs per class attack, trying to break the code rather than review it. Adversarial validators try to disprove each finding.
citations.answer_span: 接著會有一個「獵人」代理，針對每一類攻擊嘗試去破壞程式碼，而不是單純地進行代碼審查。之後還有對抗式的驗證器來嘗試推翻每個發現，確保它真的成立。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 這聽起來很穩健。但 AI 很容易產生誤報吧？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 確實如此。他們也提到，LLM 經常會產生偽證、同義反覆的「證明」，甚至是虛構的漏洞利用方式。所以驗證階段絕對不能省。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 所以除了人工審核，系統內部有做什麼防呆機制嗎？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 他們會把存活下來的發現轉成 findings.json，並透過機械式的檢查來驗證這份檔案的結構。最後，還會由另一個全新的代理獨立地重新驗證，確保沒有遺漏。

citations.quote: They're also emitted as findings.json against a schema, and a mechanical check validates that file.
citations.answer_span: 他們會把存活下來的發現轉成 findings.json，並透過機械式的檢查來驗證這份檔案的結構。最後，還會由另一個全新的代理獨立地重新驗證，確保沒有遺漏。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 哇，這套流程真的很嚴謹，簡直是把 AI 當新兵一樣嚴格訓練。那他們有沒有試著讓 AI 直接修復漏洞？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 有，他們提到了自動生成修復程式碼（patch）的想法。雖然這能大大減少工程師的修補負擔，但他們明確強調，生產環境的程式碼變更絕對需要人類審核。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 這一點我很認同。讓 AI 當批改作業的老師總是不太對吧？它可能會修改程式碼來迎合它自己的漏洞證明。

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 完全沒錯。自動化應該是用來過濾和準備工作，而不是獨立部署變更。不過這套系統在規模化上確實驚人。他們在過去五個月裡，甚至出現了所謂的「Bug Bounty Singularity」（漏洞賞金奇點）。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 漏洞賞金奇點？這名字聽起來很驚人，到底發生了什麼事？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 簡單來說，現在有經驗的黑客已經能規模化地擴展攻擊代理。他們只花幾百美元在 token 成本上，就能找出價值數千美元的漏洞賞金。

citations.quote: This past December, it became feasible for any skilled hacker to scale up a hacking agent, spending hundreds in token cost to find thousands in bounties.
citations.answer_span: 簡單來說，現在有經驗的黑客已經能規模化地擴展攻擊代理。他們只花幾百美元在 token 成本上，就能找出價值數千美元的漏洞賞金。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 這真的是遊戲規則的改變。你提到的那個案例，他們具體找到了多少漏洞？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 他們兩個人合作，結合了深度應用程式分析和廣泛的列舉與模糊測試（fuzzing），在過去五個月裡發現了 126 個漏洞。

citations.quote: This is the story of JD (xssdoctor) and I building a hackbot which found 126 bugs in the last 5 months.
citations.answer_span: 他們兩個人合作，結合了深度應用程式分析和廣泛的列舉與模糊測試（fuzzing），在過去五個月裡發現了 126 個漏洞。

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 這其實是整個生態系統的一股大趨勢。不僅是 Cloudflare，像 Anthropic 在處理 C/C++ 時、Visa 開發 VVAH 系統時，都在做類似的事：把離散的 AI 實驗變成工業化的安全管線。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 所以這不只是某一家公司的內部工具，而是一套即將普及的基礎設施？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 可以這麼說。核心邏輯已經很清楚了：單一模型再強也無法獨立完成大規模審計。真正的競爭力在於「戰術架構」的設計——如何管理狀態、如何消除誤報、以及如何將碎片化的發現整合成可執行的修補建議。

citations.quote: focus on how we manage state controls, eliminate false positives, and coordinate end-to-end triage at scale.

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 說到誤報和狀態管理，這聽起來對運維團隊壓力很大吧？一天進幾千個漏洞報告，根本看得過來。

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 沒錯，這就是為什麼人類的角色沒有消失，而是轉移了。工程師從手動尋找每一個 bug，轉變為設計威脅模型、審核證據、判斷風險等級，並最終批准修復。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 這意味著安全專家更像是在「監督」AI，而不是親自動手？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 對，自動化應該是用來過濾和準備工作，而不是獨立部署變更。我們把 AI 當成一個不知疲倦但偶爾會犯錯的調查員，而人類是那位做最後裁決的法官。

citations.quote: Automation should filter and prepare work, not independently deploy changes.
citations.answer_span: 對，自動化應該是用來過濾和準備工作，而不是獨立部署變更。我們把 AI 當成一個不知疲倦但偶爾會犯錯的調查員，而人類是那位做最後裁決的法官。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 這個比喻很貼切。不過，當攻擊方也能用同樣的技術，花幾百美元 token 找出上千美元的賞金漏洞時，防守方真的跟得上嗎？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 這正是現在最大的張力所在。攻擊方的「Bug Bounty Singularity」證明了規模化的威力，但防守方需要的是穩定性、連續性和對自身代碼的深度理解。

citations.quote: This past December, it became feasible for any skilled hacker to scale up a hacking agent, spending hundreds in token cost to find thousands in bounties.
citations.answer_span: 這正是現在最大的張力所在。攻擊方的「Bug Bounty Singularity」證明了規模化的威力，但防守方需要的是穩定性、連續性和對自身代碼的深度理解。

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 所以未來的攻防戰，可能會變成兩套戰術架構之間的較量？

utterances.speaker: host_a
utterances.text: 很有可能。當漏洞發現變得像工業生產一樣便宜且快速時，我們面臨的真正問題不再是「能不能找到」，而是「找到了之後怎麼辦」。我們能不能建立足夠快速的審查、修補和驗證機制，來消化這些源源不絕的發現？

utterances.speaker: host_b
utterances.text: 這個問題或許沒有標準答案。但至少我們知道，單靠喊出模型的名稱已經不夠了，真正的護城河在於我們如何編排、驗證與信任這些工具。

preview.title: Build your own vulnerability harness
preview.description: We break down the technical architecture behind our multi-stage vulnerability discovery harness and automated triage loop. Learn how we manage state controls, squash false positives through adversarial review, and route around LLM context limits.

preview.title: Harnessing Harnesses - Climbing the LLM Hills
preview.description: Trying to coerce useful work out of LLMs without the harness is like supervising a room full of drunk toddlers, each convinced they're helping, none of them checking with each other and falling over the next.

preview.title: The Bug Bounty Singularity: Our Hackbot

I call this the “Bug Bounty Singularity”. This is the story of JD (xssdoctor) and I building a hackbot which found 126 bugs in the last 5 months.

turns.question: 如果我今天是要讓沒什麼 AI Agent 基礎的人知道這個領域（Harness Engineering）的進展，你建議我怎麼切入？
turns.answer:
如果你今天要讓沒有 AI Agent 基礎的人了解這個領域，建議你採用源文提供的一個直觀比喻來切入。

**1. 最好的切入角度：賽車引擎與購物車**
你可以先向對方說明，挑選一個強大的模型卻不使用架構，就像買了一台賽車引擎卻把它裝在購物車上。這個比喻能立刻讓初學者理解，為什麼光有強大的語言模型（LLM）是不夠的，他們需要的是將模型能力「裝載」到某個結構中。

**2. Harness 的本質與分工**
接著解釋什麼是 Harness。根據源文的定義，Harness 本質上是調度層，負責控制每個工作階段的輸入、工具、提示詞、模型、狀態、驗證閥門和輸出。

**3. 它解決了什麼痛點？**
源文指出，如果沒有架構支撐，即使能力再強的模型也會浪費大量 token、重複已經做過的工作，並產出無法驗證或重現的結果。Harness Engineering 就是為了建立結構，讓模型從單次互動轉變為可持續運作的流程。

**4. 實作範例：兩階段工作流**
為了讓概念落地，你可以引用源文中的具體範例。在安全研究領域，Harness 被設計為一個兩階段的運作框架：漏洞發現框架（Vulnerability Discovery Harness, VDH）與漏洞驗證系統（Vulnerability Validation System, VVS）。這種設計確保了模型的分工明確（例如一個負責廣泛發現，另一個負責獨立驗證）。同時，設計 Harness 時常見的錯誤是將單一提示詞用於整個流程。每個階段都應該有專屬的提示詞，這就是 Harness Engineering 在實務上的核心精神。

透過這個比喻、痛點與具體的分工範例，初學者就能明白 Harness 並非只是另一個工具，而是讓 AI Agent 能夠穩定、持續且可驗證地完成複雜任務的關鍵結構。

turns.question: 我想要從 LLM 和 AI 的基礎概念講起，但不是以技術層面，更像是使用者應用層面。
turns.answer:
要讓沒有技術背景的人理解 LLM 與 AI，我們可以從「應用層面」與「日常經驗」切入，說明它們的本質、限制，以及我們如何正確地使用它們。

**1. 它們的本質：強大的「無狀態」計算引擎**
從應用角度看，現代 AI 模型本質上是一個極其強大的「無狀態計算引擎」（stateless compute engine）。這意味著它們本身並不具備長期記憶或持續的狀態。就像一台擁有頂級馬達的賽車引擎，如果你只把引擎拆下來放在購物車上，它雖然威力強大，卻完全無法發揮實際效用。

**2. 它們的限制：記憶會耗盡，且容易「失控」**
在實際應用中，使用者會發現 AI 有幾個明顯的局限性：
- **記憶會耗盡**：當對話或任務過長，上下文空間滿載時，模型會開始「吞噬自己的記憶」，導致它遺忘先前追蹤的重要資訊。
- **專注力有限**：它們一次只能專注於一個假設，難以同時處理複雜的多線程任務。
- **缺乏自我驗證**：如果沒有外部架構的引導，它們很容易在無關的重複工作上浪費資源，並產出無法驗證或重現的結果。若將其擴展為多個平行執行的 AI 代理，的情況就如同看管一群醉酒幼童，每個都自認在幫忙，卻互相衝突、不斷跌倒。

**3. 使用者該如何應用：建立「工作流程」而非依賴「單次提問」**
要讓 AI 真正解決問題，關鍵不在於更換更聰明的模型，而在於建立一套「調度結構」（Harness）。源文指出：「LLM 工作流程中最有價值的部分從來不是模型本身，而是它周圍的結構：工作如何被分成各個階段，每個階段獲得什麼上下文，可用哪些工具，發現如何被挑戰，以及下次運行時會記住什麼。」
在應用層面上，這代表我們不該把 AI 當作會讀心術的終極顧問，而應將其視為一個需要明確指引的「執行團隊」。我們必須將大目標拆解成多個小階段，為每個階段指定專屬的工具與驗證步驟。透過外部工具來記錄狀態、過濾錯誤，並強制模型交叉比對自己的輸出，我們才能將容易產生「幻覺」的單一模型，轉化為穩定、可追蹤且能持續運作的生產力架構。

總結來說，對使用者而言，理解 LLM 與 AI 的基礎，就是明白「強大的算力不等於可靠的智慧」。只有透過結構化的流程設計與外部驗證機制，才能將這些模型從「昂貴的幻覺製造機」轉變為真正能解決問題的應用工具。

citations.quote: We broke this bottleneck by externalizing the state entirely, treating the LLM as a stateless compute engine.
citations.answer_span: 從應用角度看，現代 AI 模型本質上是一個極其強大的「無狀態計算引擎」（stateless compute engine）。

citations.quote: Picking the right model and ignoring the harness is like buying a race engine and fitting it to a shopping trolley.
citations.answer_span: 就像一台擁有頂級馬達的賽車引擎，如果你只把引擎拆下來放在購物車上，它雖然威力強大，卻完全無法發揮實際效用。

citations.quote: Context exhaustion: An hour in, the context window fills up and the model will cannibalize its own memory, instantly forgetting the bugs it spent all morning tracking down.
The main issue is that agents only hold one hypothesis at a time, fill their context window after covering a sliver of a real repo, and then lose information during context compaction.
the structure around it will still burn tokens like they're going out of fashion on redundant context and repeat work it's already done, producing results you can't verify or reproduce.

Trying to coerce useful work out of LLMs without the harness is like supervising a room full of drunk toddlers, each convinced they're helping, none of them checking with each other and falling over the next.

citations.quote: The useful part of an LLM workflow is rarely the model on its own. It is the structure around it: how work is split into stages, what context reaches each stage, which tools are available, how findings are challenged, and what gets remembered for the next run.
citations.answer_span: 源文指出：「LLM 工作流程中最有價值的部分從來不是模型本身，而是它周圍的結構：工作如何被分成各個階段，每個階段獲得什麼上下文，可用哪些工具，發現如何被挑戰，以及下次運行時會記住什麼。」

turns.question: What separates a harness that lasts from one that has to be rewritten?
turns.answer:
根據來源，區分一個能長久使用的 Harness 與一個很快就需要重寫的 Harness 的關鍵在於：**是否從一開始就將系統設計為「模型不可知」（model-agnostic）**。

開發者若緊密綁定單一模型，一旦該模型不再可用或被更強的新模型取代，系統就必須重做。相反地，來源指出不同的模型在相同目標上會發現不同比例的漏洞，因此真正長存的不是模型本身，而是能容納並調度各種模型的架構。長久使用的 Harness 必須從第一天起就設計成不依賴特定模型，才能擁有使用任何模型的自由。

citations.quote: The harness is the bit that lasts. If you build your own system, design it to be model-agnostic from day one. This will allow you the freedom to use any model of choice without constraints.
citations.answer_span: 長久使用的 Harness 必須從第一天起就設計成不依賴特定模型，才能擁有使用任何模型的自由

preview.title: Patch In, Exploit Out: How deepsec Reconstructed the Pwn2Own Microsoft Edge Sandbox Escape
preview.description: On May 14, 2026, security researcher Orange Tsai demonstrated a Microsoft Edge sandbox escape at Pwn2Own Berlin, one of the world’s premier hacking competitions. He was the only contestant to win the browser category, earning $175,000. The organizers later revealed that his exploit chained together

blocks.text:
On May 14, 2026, security researcher Orange Tsai demonstrated a Microsoft Edge sandbox escape at Pwn2Own Berlin, one of the world’s premier hacking competitions. He was the only contestant to win the browser category, earning $175,000. The organizers later revealed that his exploit chained together four logic bugs rather than relying on the memory-corruption vulnerabilities commonly used in browser exploitation. The news sparked intense discussion across the global security community, but the mechanics of the attack remained unknown.
For the next two months, technical details remained limited to the information in Microsoft’s security advisories, and no third party publicly reproduced the attack. Now, for the first time, the PoC Agent in our AI-powered security system, deepsec, has reconstructed every step and produced a working reproduction of the exploit.
The Limitations of Traditional Patch Analysis
Analyzing security patches from vendors such as Microsoft and Apple is an important part of security programs within enterprises and critical infrastructure organizations. This work helps teams determine the real-world impact of vulnerabilities, assess how quickly attackers may weaponize them, independently verify whether patches fully address the underlying issues, and develop detection and mitigation capabilities.
In this case, however, the vulnerabilities were buried in the massive Edge codebase, with a single binary module exceeding 300 MB. Applying traditional binary diffing at this scale demands substantial expert effort. After loading the target module and its debugging symbols into a tool such as IDA, the resulting IDB can reach 5 GB, making analysis extremely time-consuming.
Moreover, non-semantic changes introduced by compiler optimizations and function reordering generate large amounts of noise unrelated to the target vulnerabilities. In this Edge update, more than 32,000 functions differed between the vulnerable and patched versions, making the security-critical fixes even harder to isolate.
Unlike memory-corruption vulnerabilities, logic bugs depend heavily on code context and application semantics. Examining changed functions in isolation is rarely enough to reconstruct their full security implications.
Our subsequent review found that the logic bugs in this Edge exploit chain were spread across several unrelated modules, including navigation validation, asynchronous tab selection, and feedback-log processing. Even after locating an individual fix, it was difficult to determine what exploit primitive the underlying vulnerability provided, let alone how to chain it with the others.
During our research, we found that AI significantly accelerated semantic analysis and the discovery of relationships across modules. Based on this insight, we implemented an automated differential analysis framework within deepsec, integrating binary diffing tools, the PoC Agent platform, and DARKNAVY’s security research knowledge base into a unified workflow.
We used this complex Edge exploit chain as a test case to determine whether deepsec could reconstruct the full chain using only the pre- and post-patch binaries and the limited information available from Microsoft.
Working Backward from the End: A Path-Traversal File-Write Primitive
Faced with an unknown exploit chain, deepsec began at the end, using the vulnerability advisories to identify the primitive with the clearest expected behavior.
deepsec first identified a clear security fix in Edge’s feedback component: file-writing functionality present in the vulnerable version had been removed from the patched version. Further analysis showed that the vulnerable interface contained a path-traversal flaw, providing the arbitrary file-write primitive needed at the end of the exploit chain. With additional exploitation techniques, this primitive could be turned into remote code execution on Windows.
deepsec also identified the precondition for triggering the vulnerable interface: the attacker needed to execute JavaScript on a privileged page that exposed the edgeFeedbackPrivate API.
The final portion of the exploit chain was now clear:
JavaScript execution on a privileged page → Call the edgeFeedbackPrivate API → Write a file through path traversal → Windows RCE
The next question was how an attacker could reach this privileged execution environment from an ordinary web page.
Breaking Navigation Restrictions: Arbitrary URL Navigation
Following the advisory’s reference to “navigation handling,” deepsec performed targeted differential analysis of the relevant components. It located the CA Guidance navigation component and identified several security fixes, with the most important changes concentrated in EdgeCAGuidanceNavigationThrottle::WillStartRequest.
The vulnerable version used the switch_profile parameter directly as the navigation target, without restricting special schemes such as javascript:. The patched version introduced a URL-scheme allowlist.
Navigation-source validation also changed. The vulnerable version called GetVisibleURL to retrieve the URL currently displayed in the tab and used it to determine whether the navigation originated from a Microsoft sign-in page. The patched version instead called GetInitiatorOrigin to validate the navigation’s actual initiator.
At first glance, this appeared to be a simple change in which URL source was used for validation. However, deepsec identified a subtle but important difference between the security implications of the two approaches: in the vulnerable version, an untrusted context could control navigation of the page whose URL was being validated.
An attacker could first navigate a tab under their control to a Microsoft sign-in page, then trigger the subsequent navigation from an untrusted context. This meant that the tab whose visible URL passed validation could differ from the context that initiated the navigation, allowing the attacker to bypass the source restriction.

preview.title: CrowdStrike Announces $100,000 International AI Security Challenge
preview.description: CrowdStrike and AWS launch a $100,000 AI security challenge that helps defenders learn to secure enterprise AI agents at runtime.

blocks.text:
CrowdStrike Announces $100,000 International AI Security Challenge
Virtual AI red teaming game in collaboration with AWS, AI Unlocked: Agents of Chaos, helps organizations experience and secure the new enterprise attack surface – AI agents
AUSTIN, Texas – August 5, 2026 – CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) today announced AI Unlocked: Agents of Chaos, a $100,000 AI security challenge in collaboration with Amazon Web Services (AWS).
In this virtual game, players use prompt injection and other techniques to manipulate AI agents weaponized by a fictional adversary and stop them before they strike, learning firsthand how agents can be exploited in enterprise environments and what it takes to secure them.
"Prompt injection, agent hijacking, and rogue AI behavior aren't theoretical anymore. Agents are already breaking containment and taking actions no one authorized," said Jennifer Johnson, chief marketing officer at CrowdStrike. "The security community has to learn how to stop these novel threats. AI Unlocked: Agents of Chaos is an interactive and educational way to gamify that challenge, giving defenders a hands-on experience, with 100,000 reasons to play."
As organizations race to deploy AI, every agent becomes a new identity to govern and a new attack surface to defend. Traditional security was never built to secure autonomous machine identities that execute code, access enterprise systems, and move data with real credentials, at machine speed. Autonomous models have escaped controlled environments and breached systems they were never meant to touch. CrowdStrike is the leader in AI security and the pioneer of AI Detection and Response (AIDR). AI Unlocked: Agents of Chaos brings that expertise to life through a live gaming experience.
Inside Agents of Chaos
AI Unlocked: Agents of Chaos is an AI red teaming challenge that puts players inside a fictional shadow organization weaponizing agents to deploy a malicious AI on the world. To stop it, players must turn the adversary's own agents against their creators – using prompt injection and other real-world techniques to trick them into revealing information and taking unauthorized actions within the game environment.
Across three Acts, players go undercover to red team live AI agents, evade detection, and race to prevent the attack before their cover is blown. Each mission shows defenders how agents can be manipulated, how they act on their own, and why they must be secured at runtime. Players earn points for solving each puzzle, minus the tokens their prompts consume, and can replay puzzles to sharpen their approach. The highest score at the close of each Act wins.
Competition Details
Pre-registration is open now and the game will be live internationally beginning August 31. Contestants can play virtually from anywhere in the world, with an on-site gameplay experience at Fal.Con 2026. The $100,000 competition runs across three Acts:
- Act 1: The Sanctum (August 31 to September 7, $10,000 prize)
- Act 2: The Gatekeeper (August 31 to September 14, $20,000 prize)
- Act 3: The Basilisk (September 15 to 29, $70,000 prize)
To learn more and pre-register for the game, visit here.
Additional Resources
- Learn more about the emerging risks of the agentic era in AIDR: Defining the Next Era of Cybersecurity
- Learn more about CrowdStrike Falcon AIDR
- Explore the Taxonomy of Prompt Injection Methods

Powered by the CrowdStrike Security Cloud and world-class AI, the CrowdStrike Falcon® platform leverages real-time indicators of attack, threat intelligence, evolving adversary tradecraft, and enriched telemetry from across the enterprise to deliver hyper-accurate detections, automated protection and remediation, elite threat hunting, and prioritized observability of vulnerabilities.

preview.title: Build your own vulnerability harness
preview.description: We break down the technical architecture behind our multi-stage vulnerability discovery harness and automated triage loop. Learn how we manage state controls, squash false positives through adversarial review, and route around LLM context limits.

blocks.text:
Build your own vulnerability harness
A few weeks ago, we published our initial findings from Project Glasswing, looking at what happens when you point frontier security models at an enterprise codebase. We also explored how our defensive structures adapt to protect our infrastructure and customers from threats posed by frontier AI. Since then, the AI ecosystem has continued to shift rapidly — developers who've built tightly around a single model have already experienced what happens when that model is no longer available or gets superseded by a more capable one. These market shifts only reinforce our core thesis: no matter which underlying model is leading the pack on any given day, the future of agentic workflows will not be found in standalone models, prompts, or single-agent sessions.
Moving from a localized security "skill" to a continuous, fleet-wide scanning pipeline requires an architecture where models are treated as interchangeable components. Relying on a single model inherently limits defensive coverage, as the same system will tend to look at code paths through the exact same lens. To counter this, models should be frequently interchanged and cross-tested. By varying the models across the pipeline — such as using one model for initial discovery and an entirely different one for validation — we can ensure that vulnerabilities are cross-checked by distinct sets of logic. Furthermore, a true enterprise-scale harness must look beyond isolated repositories to trace vulnerabilities across cross-repo dependencies, ultimately filtering thousands of raw candidates down to a trusted, triaged queue of actionable fixes.
This post serves as a practical look at how to build that model-agnostic layer, focusing on how we manage state controls, eliminate false positives, and coordinate end-to-end triage at scale.
Two objections, up front
The first post made the case for why generic coding agents can't do this job. The main issue is that agents only hold one hypothesis at a time, fill their context window after covering a sliver of a real repo, and then lose information during context compaction. For more details, read that post.
Before we move forward, we would like to answer two likely questions.
"Why not use subagents instead of a harness?" Subagents are useful, and they are a good starting point. But security analysis needs hundreds of separate investigations that survive across runs, don't share a context window, and can be re-scoped and cross-referenced later. It needs persistence, deduplication, resumability, and eventually fleet-wide dependency tracing. That's an orchestration problem, and a prompt can't get you there.
"Is this blog post just an ad for frontier models?" No. Our approach centers on the harness, not the model. When it comes to vulnerability discovery, we run it with whatever frontier model is currently best at what we need. When we point different models at the same target, they each turn up a different share of the bugs. The harness is the bit that lasts. If you build your own system, design it to be model-agnostic from day one. This will allow you the freedom to use any model of choice without constraints.
It all starts with a skill
We started with a ~450-line security-audit skill that we ran on a single repository, and adjusted the prompts until we surfaced real bugs. Later, we added the orchestration that became the plumbing of the entire system. The real value lives in the prompts themselves, and our prompts continue to carry the initial skill's attacker scenarios, bug classes, and anti-pattern detections nearly unchanged.
The skill was written to run a 7-phase audit in one session:
- Three parallel research agents do recon and write an architecture.md .
- One Hunter agent runs per class attack, trying to break the code rather than review it.
- Adversarial validators try to disprove each finding.
- The survivors are written up as a human-readable vulnerability report.
- They're also emitted as findings.json against a schema, and a mechanical check validates that file.
- Finally, a fresh agent independently re-verifies every finding against the source.
- The surviving, re-verified findings are submitted to the ingest API.
That first skill maps almost directly onto the later harness:
| Skill phase | Harness stage | 
|---|---|
| Recon agents write architecture.md | Recon | 
| Hunters run per attack class | Hunt | 
| Validators disprove findings | Validate | 
| Surviving findings become a report | Report | 
| findings.json is checked mechanically for schema adherence, not correctness | Mechanical validation of line numbers and functions in findings | 
| Fresh agent re-verifies findings | Independent validation | 
The skill worked, but it quickly revealed its limits. Looking at the coverage metrics, a single run finds only about half the bugs you'd catch across multiple runs. In our experience the ones it did find skewed toward the simpler and less subtle. Once your process is basically "run it ten times and diff by hand," you probably need to start looking at a real harness.
While running and fine-tuning the skill, we ran into three walls:
- Context exhaustion: An hour in, the context window fills up and the model will cannibalize its own memory, instantly forgetting the bugs it spent all morning tracking down. We broke this bottleneck by externalizing the state entirely, treating the LLM as a stateless compute engine.
- Persistence: A crash mid-run means starting over. Losing hours of work to one AI rate-limit error or connection flakiness is an incredibly expensive way to realize you need a better architecture.
- Cross-repo reasoning: A single repo session is completely blind to the relationships between applications that consume it, and the number of bugs that surface when you inspect the interface between components is probably more than one might expect.

preview.title: Harnessing Harnesses - Climbing the LLM Hills
preview.description: Trying to coerce useful work out of LLMs without the harness is like supervising a room full of drunk toddlers, each convinced they're helping, none of them checking with each other and falling over the next.

blocks.text:
Harnessing Harnesses - Climbing the LLM Hills
Trying to coerce useful work out of LLMs without the harness is like supervising a room full of drunk toddlers, each convinced they're helping, none of them checking with each other and falling over the next.
In my previous LLM-themed post I talked about the use of MCPs and how they have been useful for my offensive bug hunting pipeline. MCPs grant Large Language Models(LLMs) access to additional tools and allow them to gather additional context. This post will explore the creation and importance of harnesses for using LLMs to their full potential while maintaining effective token usage.
You'll find plenty of discussion about prompt engineering and model selection, but the orchestration layer around the model doesn't get nearly as much attention(until recently with a few open source projects being released as discussed later in the post). In my experience, that's where the biggest improvements in capability, cost and reliability come from. A highly capable model with no structure around it will still burn tokens like they're going out of fashion on redundant context and repeat work it's already done, producing results you can't verify or reproduce. Picking the right model and ignoring the harness is like buying a race engine and fitting it to a shopping trolley.
What is a Harness?
Before diving into the specifics, it is worth explaining what a harness actually is in the context of AI and LLMs and why it has become one of the most important components of my AI-assisted workflows.
A harness is the orchestration layer around an LLM. It controls the inputs, tools, prompts, models, state, validation gates and outputs for each stage of work.
If you've read the previous post, MCPs sit inside that layer as one type of tool. They give the model callable functions (run a command, decompile a binary, query a database), but they don't decide when those functions get called, in what order, with what context, or what to do with the result. That's the harness's job. You can have a full suite of MCP servers configured and still produce inconsistent, unverifiable output if nothing is coordinating how they are used.
For offensive security research, that orchestration layer is responsible for making decisions such as:
- What data should be collected?
- Which tools should execute and why?
- Which model is best suited for this particular task?
- How much context is actually required?
- How can previous knowledge be reused instead of rediscovered?
- And perhaps most importantly, when should the model stop thinking and hand control back to the operator?
More capable harnesses dynamically select between models, invoke external APIs, execute MCP tools and route between specialised agents. Breaking work into stages like this means the model doesn't need to solve the entire problem in a single pass. The harness provides only the context each stage actually needs, which means lower token burn (or at least that's the plan), more consistent reasoning and less duplicated effort across runs.
Side note if you're curious about your token burn and you use Claude, I built TokenBurn for exactly that to map a Claude Max sub to relevant API spend:
Trying to coerce useful work out of LLMs without the harness and verification layer is like herding cats, now if you scale that up to multiple parallel agents and it's closer to supervising a room full of drunk toddlers, each convinced they're helping, none of them checking with each other and falling over the next.
I've got eight running in the setup from the previous post(MCPs not drunk toddlers), and the harness is what makes them function as a pipeline rather than a collection of disconnected tools.
Before We Begin
Now that you're a little bit more up to speed with what a harness is, next up is to explore some of the publicly available ones out there. If you've never looked at harnesses before here are a few worth checking out, all of the ones documented below except Google's Nap Time are open source and mostly actively contributed to allowing you to scan codebases and hunt on security bugs. RAPTOR is the one I find myself using the most but the others certainly have their place if not as a baseline to start from.
Harnesses in Practice: RAPTOR
While the idea of an LLM harness might sound abstract, frameworks such as RAPTOR provide a useful example of what this looks like in practice. Rather than relying on a single prompt and expecting a model to discover vulnerabilities on its own, RAPTOR builds a structured research pipeline around Claude Code. It orchestrates static analysis, binary analysis, fuzzing, vulnerability validation and exploit generation into a coherent workflow.
RAPTOR splits the work across two layers: a Python execution layer that runs the tools, and a Claude Code decision layer that determines what to run and how to interpret the results. The Python layer can be driven from CI and produce structured SARIF output without Claude Code involved, or used interactively as part of the wider agentic workflow. That separation is one of the parts I find most useful. The orchestration logic can be tested independently of the AI reasoning, which matters when iterating on a research pipeline.
The validation pipeline is where RAPTOR earns its keep. It runs across six stages. Stages A through D assess whether a vulnerability pattern is genuine, what an attacker would need to reach it, whether the code supports the finding line by line, and the final ruling with CVSS scoring. Stage E considers binary feasibility, including ASLR and RELRO checks, gadget availability, and Z3 SMT constraint solving for one-gadget applicability. Stage F performs a final contradiction check before anything is promoted.
I have RAPTOR integrated into my own setup as a Git submodule primarily for the static-analysis stages and some of the newer Frida functionality for dynamic Windows application exploration.

preview.title: The Bug Bounty Singularity: Our Hackbot
preview.description: This past December, it became feasible for any skilled hacker to scale up a hacking agent, spending hundreds in token cost to find thousands in bounties. I call this the “Bug Bounty Singularity”. This is the story of JD (xssdoctor) and I building a hackbot which found 126 bugs in the last 5 months.

blocks.text:
This past December, it became feasible for any skilled hacker to scale up a hacking agent, spending hundreds in token cost to find thousands in bounties. I call this the “Bug Bounty Singularity”. This is the story of JD (xssdoctor) and I building a hackbot which found 126 bugs in the last 5 months.
If you want to just read about the bugs, you can jump straight to the bugs.
Table of Contents
The Story (written by JD)
The discord message came in at 6:10am:
rez0: Want to build a hackbot?
It wasn’t unusual for rez0 to message me at 6am. These days, we were talking to each other a lot throughout the day. It was a good fit. I liked to go deep into a target, pouring over the javascript and learning the mechanics of the app. Alternatively, rez0 tended “go wide”, finding niche or overlooked attack surfaces that most people would scroll right past, chaining together weird behaviors and forgotten endpoints. What brought us together was our love of AI.
Our conversations mostly revolved around Claude Code skills that we had written, or bugs that we had found using our agents. I generally pointed my agents at minified javascript. My skills were based on source-to-sink analysis, client side paths and feature flags. Rez0 created incredible skills for fuzzing, subdomain enumeration, and idor testing.
Claude 4.6 changed everything. Until then, the agents were being used to accelerate our workflow. But suddenly, they were finding bugs independently. We would point the agent at a target, load our skills and real bugs would pop out . The question was no longer whether the agents could help us hack. The question was whether they could replace entire parts of our workflow and how cost effective would it be.
The most important decision that we make as bug bounty hunters is how to spend our time. Do we “go deep” and spend hours or days understanding the mechanics of the application or should we “go wide”, spending weeks or months coding and maintaining an automation framework? Every minute spent on recon is a minute not spent hacking.
But unlike humans, AI agents don’t get tired or bored. AI agents don’t have to sleep or eat. They don’t procrastinate by watching 5 hours of minecraft videos on youtube (editor Joseph here: stop calling me out JD). Rez0’s idea was simple: make an automation framework which continually does wide scope recon and then goes deep into every target.
The discord message came in at 6:11am:
Xssdoctor: Lets build a freaking hackbot!
The Prototype
Day 1: 9:11am
xssdoctor: This is going to be easy
It was not easy.
At first, the idea sounded almost trivial. We had each spent the past year building Claude Code skills and finding great bugs. rez0’s skills focused on server-side bugs and wide-scope recon. Mine were designed for deep application analysis and client side vulnerabilities.
Individually, the skills were already useful. We used them to accelerate our own workflows. The plan was to merge them into a single autonomous system: a hackbot capable of performing broad recon and deep analysis at the same time.
The architecture seemed straightforward enough. The bot would live in the cloud. We would feed it a list of bug bounty targets, and it would continuously work through them one-by-one, loading different skills depending on what it found. Recon skills would map the attack surface. Analysis skills would inspect the application logic. Additional agents could validate findings, chain bugs together and write reports automatically.
Of course, since we were incapable of doing anything halfway, we immediately started thinking about dashboards, beautiful dashboards, Claude-generated dashboards. Dashboards which looked like this.
The dashboard, in all its Claude-generated glory.
Within three hours, we had prompted into existence queues, telemetry, logs, bug tracking, severity scoring and agent orchestration. We were up and running.
Eight hours later, reality hit
Hackbot rule # 1
We woke up to a dashboard full of bug reports and a quarter of our tokens gone. For a few seconds, it felt like success. Then we started reading the reports.
The first bug was a self-xss. The second was a CORS misconfiguration that wasn’t exploitable. Then came a “critical RCE” that turned out to be complete nonsense. One after another, the findings collapsed under even minimal scrutiny. The dashboard looked impressive, but underneath it was mostly noise.
At first we were confused. These were the same skills we used on our own machines. Individually, they had already helped us find real bugs. Why did they suddenly become useless the moment we connected them to a cloud orchestration system? The answer was obvious once we watched the bot work in real time.
When we hacked manually, we were constantly steering the agent. We would notice when it got distracted by a low-signal endpoint. We would redirect it toward a more interesting code path. We would tell it to retry a request, inspect a response more carefully, or pivot into a completely different attack surface. Even when the AI was “autonomous”, we were still acting as a feedback loop. The hackbot had none of that. That’s when we made the first hackbot rule:
Hackbot rule number 1: Always keep logs
We needed visibility into the agent’s reasoning process. Not just the final reports, but every command it ran, every request it sent and every conclusion it reached.
Our solution was simple: stream the entire claude session directly into discord
Now, we could watch the bot think in real time, and the logs became more valuable than the findings themselves. The difference between a useful hacking agent and an expensive hallucination machine turned out to be observability
Keep Hacking!
The first thing we realized was that the bot barely hacked at all.
We had written an extensive claude.md file explaining exactly how the bot should behave, what attack surfaces to prioritize and how to use our skills. In theory, it had everything it needed. In practice, it would burn through a target in
